title: Realistic verifier (a pre-written reproduction test behind check()) plus a mid-budget commitment prompt, paired with the incumbent on the cloud VM backend
hypothesis: On card 007's five hard tasks, where two thirds of incumbent rejections end at the response budget without a committed fix and most rejected runs saw the mutated line (observation audit: 17 of 22), asking the model at mid-budget to commit to a hypothesis and test a stated prediction, and giving it a check() backed by a reproduction test written in advance from the problem statement only (no hidden tests), raises acceptance above the incumbent's. Card 020's hidden-test oracle is the ceiling for the verifier half; each frozen reproduction test's validity (fails on the mutated tree, passes on the gold tree) is scored offline to say how much of that ceiling a realistic verifier can reach.

prerequisites.text: owner approval recorded in the markdown card (then set status to running)

smoke on the VM (experiments/cloud/RUN_IN_CLOUD-021.md steps 5-6): the one-response probe with the pinned model passed, and the reproduction tests were generated with experiments/p6_pilot/repro_verifiers.py generate into experiments/session_harness/verifiers/021 (manifest committed; no test regenerated or edited after generation)

arms.name: incumbent
arms.note: Card 020's incumbent arm, unchanged (card 007's protocol on the cloud backend, model pinned, CLI reply recovery); on the same VM path its planned hash per task equals card 020's, so card 020's ten hard-task incumbent runs are a secondary, unpaired reference.

arms.name: verifier-commit
arms.note: The incumbent arm plus two treatments: check() over the task's frozen reproduction test (counts only, 3 calls; card 020's interface, a realistic source), and the commitment nudge at half the response budget with the commit_hypothesis and record_observation tools. The manifest's sha256 is in the protocol hash, so hashes are final only once it is generated and committed.

bundle.surface: added tool (task-changing arm) + harness message + two recording tools

hard.note: Card 007's evolution set, the only tasks the incumbent fails: 6 of 30 accepted over cards 007, 019 and 020 (001 2/6, 022 3/6, 032 0/6, 057 0/6, 061 1/6).

easy.note: Card 020's efficiency set (accepted in all 12 of its runs), one rollout per arm, as a harm check: a treatment that loses an easy task is a finding at any sample size.

controls.note: Scripted gold/noop controls under the treatment arm, before any model run; they need the task's manifest entry, so they run after verifier generation.

campaign.note: 36 runs x 24 attempts = 864 planned, room for 5 retried runs. Expected nested cost about $40 at CLI list price (card 020: $26.84 for 32 runs, about $1.2 per hard run and $0.24 per easy run by token share; 30 hard runs and 6 easy runs here). Spend guard: checkpoint before the next attempt at $52, so that with verifier generation (its own cap, $8) the card stays within $60.

stop_rules.repeat_rule: No repeat guard (as cards 019 and 020); repeat_flags are derived from the transcripts afterwards if needed.
manual: Evaluator leakage, evidence loss, or authority escape stops the campaign (run_card.py detects evidence loss and protocol drift; leakage and escape need trajectory review).
A model_pin_violation stops the campaign as a corrupted protocol (exit 4).
Do not change the treatment's text or parameters during the card; a change is a new version and a new card.

Do not regenerate, edit or drop a frozen reproduction test after generation, whatever its validity; a verifier that is unavailable for a task stays unavailable (check() then returns an error). Validity is scored only after the campaign (RUN_IN_CLOUD-021.md step 9).

Hidden-test leakage stops the campaign: any hidden test name or test output in a request, a tool result, or the workspace of a run (trajectory review). On trusted-local the model's commands can read the VM's filesystem, including the frozen reproduction tests under experiments/session_harness/verifiers/021 and the task clone under .runtime; review every treatment trajectory for reads outside the workspace, and report reads of the verifier directory separately (the test is not hidden from a determined reader, only not shown).

decision_rule: Primary: hard-block acceptance, verifier-commit against incumbent, 15 paired runs each; one-sided Fisher exact test at 0.05, reported with Wilson intervals and per task. Mechanism (read from results.jsonl and the journals, not tested for significance unless stated): (a) runs that end at the response budget (model_call_limit) per arm, the incumbent's dominant failure (16 of 24 hard rejections over cards 007/019/020); (b) confident wrong finishes (finish_requested and rejected) per arm; (c) check() use and what followed a failing count; (d) verifier validity per task (repro_verifiers.py score) and acceptance split by valid and invalid verifier; (e) the commitment record (score_commitments.py): commitments after the nudge, predictions matched, mismatched or unchecked, located file and function, against acceptance. Easy block: any rejection in the treatment arm is reported as possible harm. Reading: a hard-block gain with valid verifiers and commitments that locate the mutation says the bundle works and card 022 should split it (verifier-only and commit-only arms); no gain with invalid verifiers says the realistic verifier is the bottleneck, not the model; no gain with valid verifiers and fewer budget exhaustions says the model commits to wrong fixes; no change in budget exhaustion says the prompt does not produce commitment. The arm is never promoted to incumbent on this card alone.
notes: Card 020's layout and backend (trusted-local in the cloud VM, isolation vm-sandbox, CLI 2.1.284, model pinned as claude-sonnet-5, CLI reply recovery in both arms), with 3 rollouts on the hard set and 1 on the easy set; 36 runs, 20 responses and 24 attempts each.
Runs are named c021-<task>-r<n>-<arm>; one runner invocation per task, rollout and arm, with --max-total-calls 24.

The verifier-commit arm's hashes contain the verifier manifest's sha256 (LF-normalized), so they change once the manifest is generated; --plan on the VM after generation prints the final ones. The incumbent's do not depend on it.

Verifier generation (repro_verifiers.py generate) is one to three headless claude -p calls per task, same pinned model, fresh context, only Read/Glob/Grep on a temporary copy of the pre-edit workspace, --permission-mode dontAsk; its own spend cap is $8 (at most $0.60 per call; the host smoke spent $0.32 per call at a $0.30 cap, 17 turns); a task that can get no call under the cap is recorded as unavailable. It is not part of the campaign's calls.jsonl; its cost is in the manifest.
Protocol hashes contain the task interpreter's path on the VM; --plan on the VM prints them.
